story.head: The Sabres better keep their heads up
paras: The Sabres have won three straight, and the Senators (9-5-1) beat San Jose 5-1 on Saturday. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Senators third (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Sabres seventh (tied for 13th). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Senators’ record (.633) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.563), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. So is the Sabres’ (.607 on chances worth .540), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games.

The Senators (2nd) and the Sabres (3rd) both rarely get pinned in their own end. The Sens play slow, tight games (3rd lowest) and draw more penalties than they take (4th). On the other side, the Sabres don't block many shots (29th). They also get their shots through better than almost anyone (3rd), and their knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot. The Senators hit a lot, but the Sabres mostly don’t.

Tim Stützle (9 G / 12 A / 21 P in 15 GP) leads the Senators in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. Drake Batherson (9 G / 8 A / 17 P in 15 GP) is next in line, with ten points in his last five games. For the Sabres, Tage Thompson (10 G / 7 A / 17 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games and eight goals in eleven games against Ottawa since 2023-24. Jack Quinn (8 G / 6 A / 14 P in 14 GP) isn’t far behind.

Jonas Johansson (1-1-0 / .859 SV% in 3 GS) will likely start for Ottawa. Buffalo has two options in net: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (4-3-3 / .873 SV% in 9 GS) and Colten Ellis (3-1-0 / .880 SV% in 5 GS). Luukkonen has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Saturday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
